full_judgment: 6. Mr. Abdus Salam, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has contended that as in the recent settlement operation the suit land was recorded as “সাধারণের ব্যবহার্য” bhiti land the court of appeal ought to have held that the present record of right would prevail over the C.S. record. In support of his contention Mr. Salam has cited Bhupendra Krishna Chose V. Abdur Rahman reported in 51 C.L.J 18 where it has been held that in a conflict between the old record of rights, and a recent record of rights, the recent record is to be presumed to be correct unless it is proved by evidence to be incorrect and the burden of proof to show that it is incorrect is upon the party challenging it. In Abhiram Bedanta V. Chintamani Bedamia reported in 100 I.C. 1927 (701), cited by Mr. Satan it has been held that when there are two records of rights prepared at different times, entries in both of them will be presumed to be correct entries of facts existing at the time the entries were made and that there is nothing in the law which would entitle a party to say that the entry in the sub-sequent record is rebutted by the entry in the previous record.
